text: As your affection for me can only proceed from your experience and conviction of my fondness for you (for to talk of natural affection is talking nonsense), the only return I desire is, what it is chiefly your interest to make me; I mean your invariable practice of virtue, and your indefatigable pursuit of knowledge.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter III, to his son, London, December 2, Old Style 1746
